description: On May 29, 1453, after 53 days of siege, the Ottomans forced the walls of Constantinople. The New Rome fell, and the Middle Ages tipped into a new age.

hero.hook: A thousand years of ramparts. Fifty-three days of cannon fire. One city closing an age.

blocks.text: On **May 29, 1453**, after **53 days** of siege, the soldiers of the Ottoman sultan entered **Constantinople**, capital of the Byzantine Empire, the Roman Empire of the East. The city had held out for more than a thousand years. It gave way to a new kind of artillery.
This was not only the end of Byzantium. By locking the roads to the East, the fall of the “New Rome” pushed Europe to look for other ways through. The Middle Ages closed.

Founded in **330** by the emperor Constantine, the city was for centuries the beacon of Europe. By the 15th century the Byzantine Empire was only a shadow, weakened above all by the [[sack of Constantinople by the 4th Crusade (1204)]], when Western Christian crusaders looted the city. Little was left but the capital and a few Greek lands. About **50,000** people lived among the ruins, where **500,000** souls had once lived.

blocks.caption: The Theodosian Walls, long thought impregnable

blocks.text: One asset was left: the [[Theodosian Walls]], a triple line of ramparts from the 5th century. For a thousand years nobody forced them from the land side. Constantinople was a Christian island in an Ottoman sea.
Even with the enemy at the gates, the Byzantines went on arguing about tiny points of theology. That is why we still call a hopelessly tangled debate “byzantine.”

In **1451**, **Mehmed II**, the young sultan of the Ottoman Empire, was **19 years old** and had one obsession: to take the City. He hired the founder **Urban**, who cast him the “Basilica,” a cannon **8 meters** long that fired stone balls of **600 kg**. Medieval fortifications became obsolete overnight.

blocks.caption: Mehmed II, the young sultan who wants Constantinople

blocks.text: The siege began on **April 2, 1453**. Against **80,000 to 200,000** Ottomans, including the [[Janissaries]], the sultan's elite troops, the last Byzantine emperor [[Constantine XI Palaiologos]] could field only **7,000** defenders. Every night they filled the breaches back in with wood and earth.
Urban's cannon was so heavy that it took **60 oxen** and **400 men** to move it. It could fire only **7 times** a day, or it would burst.

Blocked at the [[Golden Horn]], the city's natural harbor, by a chain stretched across the water, Mehmed had **70 ships** hauled overland behind the defenses. At dawn on **May 29**, the general assault carried a breach near the Gate of Saint Romanus. There is also a story of a small gate, the **Kerkoporta**, left open.

Constantine XI threw himself into the fighting, and his body was never formally identified. Mehmed turned **Hagia Sophia**, the great basilica, into a mosque. Constantinople became [[Istanbul]], the capital of a conquering empire.

events.detail: The young sultan prepares to take the City.
events.title: Mehmed II takes the throne

blocks.text: Greek scholars fled to Italy with their manuscripts, and the [[Greek diaspora and the Renaissance]] became a single story. In trade, the Ottomans taxed the eastern routes heavily. Portugal and Spain turned to the Atlantic. In **1492**, Columbus ran into America.

The fall ended the living continuity of [[Byzantine law and Roman heritage]]: for a thousand years Constantinople had passed on Roman law and Greek culture. Modern Europe was born partly out of that loss. A thousand-year empire went dark, and another world opened.
On **May 29, 1453**, Constantinople fell after a thousand years of resistance. The end of Byzantium, the rise of the Ottomans, a faster Renaissance and the first great voyages: it is a hinge date.
